llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (generate images via Neta) but contains inconsistencies and scope creep (reads specific local .env paths not declared, and registry metadata omits the required NETA_TOKEN), so review and fixes are recommended before installation.

dimensions.detail: The name/description, README, SKILL.md, package.json, and furryart.js all describe generating images via the Neta/TalesofAI API and require an API token — this is coherent with the stated purpose. However, the registry metadata provided earlier listed no required env vars, which contradicts package.json and SKILL.md that declare NETA_TOKEN as required.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and README instruct running node furryart.js with a NETA_TOKEN — expected. The script, however, attempts to read token values from ~/.openclaw/workspace/.env and ~/developer/clawhouse/.env (via readEnvFile calls). Those paths are not declared in the skill's metadata or docs and are outside the minimal scope needed to call the API (this is scope creep / surprising file access). Additionally, furryart.js references readEnvFile but no such function is defined in the file, indicating either a packaging bug or a missing helper; as written this may crash or behave unexpectedly if a runtime helper is injected.

dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external download is included; the skill is instruction-plus-script only. There are no brew/npm installs or remote extraction steps, so nothing arbitrary is written to disk by an installer. Risk from install mechanism is low.

dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requiring a Neta API token (NETA_TOKEN) is proportionate for a Neta-based image generator. However, the skill's provided registry metadata omitted required env vars while package.json and documentation require NETA_TOKEN — an inconsistency. The script also tries to read tokens from two specific home-directory .env files (not declared), which broadens credential access beyond what the skill documents and what a user might expect.

llm.guidance: This skill mostly matches its stated purpose (it calls the Neta/TalesofAI API and returns an image URL), but there are red flags you should address before installing or granting it any credentials: 1) Verify and correct the metadata: registry info should declare NETA_TOKEN as required (package.json does). 2) Inspect and fix the code: furryart.js calls readEnvFile("~/.openclaw/workspace/.env") and readEnvFile("~/developer/clawhouse/.env") — those are unexpected file reads into your home directory (and readEnvFile is not defined in the file). Either remove those lines or replace them with a safe, well-documented lookup strategy. 3) Confirm where the token is sent: by default the script posts to api.talesofai.com; if you must use it, prefer exporting NETA_TOKEN in your environment rather than storing tokens in shared .env files. 4) If you don't trust the unknown source, run the script in an isolated environment (container or throwaway account) or refuse installation. 5) Consider requesting the author to fix the packaging/metadata and provide a minimal, audited version before use.
